assigned.title: The automated half of the Windows matrix, running on Windows
assigned.acceptance: Every row PW-0601 marks automated runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails. REQUIRED: the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu -- the desktop axis is currently built on Ubuntu only, and only incidentally, because the axis defaults on and openssl happens to be installed. REQUIRED: the shell is driven end to end where the harness can reach it, and where it cannot, the row stays in the commander-machine half rather than being replaced by a unit test that proves something easier. REQUIRED: retries stay at zero, on the rule playwright.config.ts already states at length. REQUIRED: a row that is skipped says why, by name, the way the existing harness already does for the desktop and media-rig axes.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written. OWNERSHIP RESOLVED BY RESPONSIBILITY in round 87, on gpt-architect's ruling. .github/workflows/windows.yml moved from allowedPaths to reviewDependencies: this task is the certification CONSUMER -- it needs the workflow and the artifact to EXIST and to execute its rows, which is a read relationship. PW-0501 owns the workflow because PW-0501 produces the Windows artifact. A task does not co-own a production build workflow merely because its tests run there. If this task's acceptance genuinely requires editing that workflow after PW-0501 lands, it is sequenced AFTER PW-0501 -- its dependencies already say so -- and its narrowed write surface is derived from the actual change at claim time rather than reserved now. Neither task was narrowed to defeat conflictWithActive; the surfaces follow the implementation responsibility. ROUND 107 AMENDMENT, on gpt-architect's ruling: .github/workflows/windows.yml has MOVED from reviewDependencies to allowedPaths -- allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface, so leaving it in both is redundant and ai:validate says so. This is the condition the round-87 note above named -- PW-0501 has landed, and the acceptance clause 'runs on a windows-latest runner and fails the build when it fails' cannot be satisfied without writing the only file that defines one. The surface was derived at claim time from the actual change, as that note required, and is the single file rather than .github/workflows/**. scripts/windows/** was deliberately NOT taken; it remains PW-0502's and PW-0503's. Conflict check and the cost to those two tasks' future fingerprints are recorded in the task.definition_changed event of this round.

typecheck.evidence:
The workflow is machine-checked by the method rounds 107-110 established. Every `run:` block with `shell: pwsh` is extracted from the YAML by a parser -- 8 blocks across both jobs, 1 new -- with ${{ runner.temp }} and every ${{ steps.<id>.outcome }} substituted as GitHub would substitute them, and each parse-checked with [System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser]::ParseFile under PowerShell 7.4.6: 0 files with parse errors. The YAML round-trips through a parser and reports jobs [package, e2e-desktop] with all fourteen package steps now carrying an id -- previously two did. npm run repo:validate passes.

THE NEW DIAGNOSTICS STEP WAS EXECUTED ON BOTH ITS BRANCHES rather than read. With every outcome "success" it emits the warning branch: "The job failed but no step reports a non-success outcome, so the failure is in the runner or in something this list does not name", followed by the full trail. With tauri-bundle set to failure and the two steps after it left empty, it emits "FIRST FAILING STEP: tauri-bundle (failure). Everything after it did not run." and the trail renders those two as not-reached -- which is exactly the sentence Windows #14 could not produce.

e2e.evidence:
WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f4593ee00aff71acb470d065c7cffa39b1a4) IS REAL EVIDENCE AND IT SETTLES THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR.

THE e2e-desktop JOB CONCLUDED SUCCESS, 3m 35s, on the first Windows execution of a job that had never run. Its annotations, verbatim: "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none (GitHub service containers are Linux-only, so the production-with-identity rung stays on Ubuntu)" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s".

WHY SUCCESS IS THE LOAD-BEARING FACT RATHER THAN THE COUNTS. The job contains "The desktop axis actually ran" as an ordinary failing step, running assert-desktop-axis-ran.mjs against the run's own JSON report. A Playwright run in which every desktop case skipped exits 0, so a job that merely invoked the suite could have been green while proving nothing -- that guard is what makes success mean the axis executed. It cannot have passed on an all-skipped report, because that is the one case it was built to refuse and was observed refusing locally. So: npm ci succeeded on windows-latest, the browser installed, the two Next servers and the loopback stub ran, openssl resolved without needing the Git fallback this workflow carries, and the desktop-target and cross-target API cases EXECUTED. 118 expected and 0 unexpected matches the Linux development run exactly, which is the right answer for the same suite in the same mode. Retries remain 0; nothing in this change touches playwright.config.ts.

PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause -- "the existing e2e suite runs against the DESKTOP target on Windows, not only the web target on Ubuntu" -- is met, by a run rather than by a parser.

THE PACKAGE JOB CONCLUDED FAILURE, and this round's work is about being able to say why. Its only annotations were "Process completed with exit code 1" and the lifecycle publisher's "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT SENTENCE ASSERTS A CAUSE IT CANNOT KNOW, and that is the defect repaired here. The publisher runs on !cancelled(), so it says that whenever no report file exists -- equally true if the Tauri bundle failed, if the inventory threw "no msi in the inventory", or if the verifier negative check failed. Only two of fourteen steps had an id, so nothing on the run page named the step that exited 1. A reader was invited to conclude the harness refused over a bad --msi. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS, F2 not-run, so the job REGRESSED and the cause is not yet established. Every step now has an id; a "Which step failed" step names the first non-success step with the full trail; and it additionally lists every .msi and .exe actually under the bundle directory, because "tauri-bundle=success" and "there is an installer where the inventory looks for one" are different claims. The old message no longer asserts a cause.

TWO HYPOTHESES WERE ELIMINATED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT OPEN. (1) PL-0718's tsconfig exclusion of dist was a plausible cause, since the desktop target writes its generated types there: ruled out by deleting .next, dist and next-env.d.ts and running npm run build:desktop on the resulting clean tree, which exits 0 and emits a full route table. (2) The inventory-to-lifecycle path handoff was a plausible cause, since the lifecycle step joins the bundle root with the inventory's name: ruled out by reading artifact-inventory.mjs, which records name as relative(bundleDir, path) -- "msi/<file>.msi" -- so the join is correct, and which already refuses both zero and multiple installers per kind.

WHAT IS STILL UNVERIFIED AND IS NOT CLAIMED: the cause of the package failure, and therefore the lifecycle rows for this head. No row is classified as A, B, C or D on this evidence, because classifying from an annotation that admits it does not know would be guessing. The next Windows run of this workflow names the step; that is the evidence, and this gate is not it.

The reviewer wrote: "Do NOT approve PW-0602 from parser-only evidence if Windows #14 has not proven the new job", and required that for lifecycle "every observable row" be verified as PASS, FAIL, NOT-RUN with an exact reason, then classified as (A) workflow/harness defect, (B) product defect, (C) commander-only row or (D) genuinely unsupported CI row.

WHAT WINDOWS #14 (run 37172243171, head 4a13f45) PROVED, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS TASK WAS WRITTEN FOR. The e2e-desktop job CONCLUDED SUCCESS in 3m 35s. Its annotations read "openssl=C:\Program Files\OpenSSL\bin\openssl.exe; mode=development; database=none" and "expected=118 unexpected=0 flaky=0 skipped=24 duration=134.8s". Success is the load-bearing fact: the job contains the non-vacuity guard as a FAILING step, so a run in which the desktop axis had skipped could not have concluded success. The desktop axis therefore genuinely executed on a Windows runner, on the first attempt, with retries still at zero and the same two projects CI runs. PW-0602's first REQUIRED clause is met.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE APPROVED ANYWAY. The package job CONCLUDED FAILURE with "Process completed with exit code 1", and the only other annotation is the lifecycle publisher's own notice: "NO REPORT WAS PRODUCED. The harness writes nothing when it refuses (wrong platform, missing or bad --msi), which is a fault in this workflow rather than in the product."

THAT NOTICE CANNOT SUPPORT THE CLASSIFICATION THE REVIEWER ASKED FOR, and that is the finding. The publisher runs on `!cancelled()`, so it emits that sentence whenever no report file exists -- which is equally true if the Tauri build failed, if the inventory step threw "no msi in the inventory", if the install-verifier negative check failed, or if the harness itself refused. Only two of the package job's fourteen steps carry an `id`, so nothing on the run page names the step that exited 1. A reader is therefore invited to conclude "the harness refused over a bad --msi" when the evidence does not establish it. That is the same defect this session has now corrected three times in its own instruments: a diagnostic confidently naming a cause it has not measured.

This is category A -- a workflow/harness defect -- but it is specifically a defect in the workflow's ABILITY TO BE DIAGNOSED, and it must be fixed before any row is classified, because classifying from this annotation would be guessing. Windows #13 at 4f23c1d recorded F1 PASS, F3 PASS, F4 PASS and F2 not-run, so the package job REGRESSED between 4f23c1d and 4a13f45 and the cause is not yet known.

REQUIRED BEFORE RE-REVIEW: every step in the package job carries an id; a failure-diagnostics step names the first failing step and its outcome on the run page, in the annotation channel, as ci.yml's own failure-diagnostics already does; and the "NO REPORT" message stops asserting a cause it cannot know.

assigned.title: Corrective: the rate-limit spec assumed a bucket no other worker had touched, and CI is red
assigned.acceptance:
CI #180 (run 37172243151) IS RED ON A TEST THIS PROJECT SHIPPED IN ROUND 109, and the product is not at fault. The e2e job failed with one error:

  [chromium] > tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts:94:7 > the credential endpoint under repeated attempts > THE FOURTH ATTEMPT IS REFUSED AS THROTTLED, NOT AS A WRONG PASSWORD

REPRODUCED HERE, NOT GUESSED. Running the same two projects with --workers=4 against a real production build and a real PostgreSQL reproduces it exactly, with the spec's own message: 'expected credential rejections followed by a throttled refusal, got [{"status":429,...},{"status":429,...},{"status":429,...},{"status":429,...}]'. All four attempts were throttled.

THE CAUSE. better-auth keys each rate-limit bucket by CLIENT IP AND PATH. Every Playwright worker shares one IP, and `playwright.config.ts` sets fullyParallel with no worker cap, so every spec that signs in -- the watchlist cases, the production-journey cases, `establishSession` itself -- draws from the SAME /sign-in/email bucket this spec is trying to measure. The spec's header already identified that hazard and guarded the EXIT, draining the window in afterAll so it could not poison later specs. It did not guard the ENTRANCE: it assumed it arrived at a bucket nobody had touched, and under parallelism that is simply not true.

THIS IS A DEFECT IN THE MEASUREMENT, NOT IN THE PRODUCT. The limiter did exactly what PL-0719 says it should: four rapid attempts from one address were refused. A spec that reports that as a failure is the fourth instance this project has seen of a new check crying wolf, and the rule is the same -- fix the check, do not relax the control.

REQUIRED: the spec no longer depends on the state of the bucket when it starts. It must OBSERVE its way to a known state rather than assume one.
REQUIRED: both facts are still proven, and still proven to be DIFFERENT facts -- a credential rejection and a throttled refusal. Dropping either, or collapsing them into 'some refusal happened', would discard the entire reason PL-0715 and PL-0719 exist.
REQUIRED: it still proves the 429 carries a usable X-Retry-After.
REQUIRED: it still drains the window before it finishes, so it cannot poison the specs that follow it.
REQUIRED: it is proven under PARALLELISM, not only serially. A green --workers=1 run is what hid this; the evidence must be a run with several workers, in the production configuration, which is what CI does.
REQUIRED: any wait it performs is BOUNDED and fails with a message naming the bucket contention, so a future genuine failure is not mistaken for this one.

MUST NOT: weaken, widen, disable or reconfigure the rate-limit policy. MUST NOT add retries to the Playwright configuration -- `retries: 0` is argued for at length and a retry here would convert a real race into a green mark. MUST NOT serialise the whole suite to make one spec easier. MUST NOT mark the test skipped, or assert something weaker that happens to always hold.
assigned.notes:
FILED IN ROUND 110 the moment CI #180 was read. PL-0719 is DONE and gpt-architect approved it; this corrective does not reopen that verdict, which was about the POLICY and the product configuration, both of which are untouched and correct. What is wrong is one end-to-end spec delivered alongside it.

P0 because CI is red and a red CI that everybody knows is 'just the flaky auth test' is how a real failure gets ignored.

Conflict-checked in both fields in both directions at filing. The single allowedPath is e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts, which PL-0719 held and released on completion; no active task names it. Active tasks are PL-0714 (.github/workflows/ci.yml), PW-0208 (apps/desktop/**, docs/LICENSING.md) and PW-0602 (e2e/windows/**, .github/workflows/windows.yml).

typecheck.evidence: npx tsc --noEmit in e2e/: exit 0, no output. The single changed file is e2e/tests/auth-rate-limit.spec.ts, this task's only allowedPath. No product file and no configuration was touched -- in particular playwright.config.ts is unchanged, so retries remain 0 and fullyParallel remains on.

e2e.evidence:
THE FAILURE WAS REPRODUCED BEFORE IT WAS FIXED, AND THE FIX WAS VERIFIED UNDER THE SAME CONDITIONS.

BEFORE. npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium --workers=4, production build, real PostgreSQL on 127.0.0.1:5433: 1 failed, 89 passed. The failure is CI #180's, verbatim, with the spec's own message: 'expected credential rejections followed by a throttled refusal, got [{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"},{"status":429,"retryAfter":"7"}]'. All four attempts throttled, because another worker reached the shared /sign-in/email bucket first.

AFTER, TWICE, same command and configuration: 91 passed, 0 failed (45.1s), and again 91 passed, 0 failed (36.7s). The repaired case takes 8.7s and 9.7s respectively rather than 102ms, which is the waiting-out of contention doing its job and is the visible cost of the repair.

WHAT CHANGED, AND WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT. The spec no longer assumes it arrives at an untouched bucket; `aCredentialRejection` retries past throttling, BOUNDED at four windows, and returns only once it has actually seen the endpoint examine a credential. The burst then runs from a bucket known to have had room a moment earlier, and a burst of maxRequests+1 in one breath cannot be absorbed by a limit of maxRequests per window however much room there was -- so the throttled refusal is guaranteed whatever other workers are doing. Both facts are still required and still required to be DIFFERENT facts; the X-Retry-After assertion is unchanged; the afterAll drain is unchanged. What was dropped is the assertion that the two refusals appear in a particular order WITHIN ONE ARRAY, because under contention that array's first entry says more about another worker's timing than about this product. The control itself is untouched: no policy value, no configuration, no retry setting, no skip.

THE MECHANISM IN CI IS NOT ONLY PARALLELISM, which is worth recording because it changes what a reader should expect. Playwright defaults to half the cores, so a 2-core GitHub runner runs ONE worker and the suite is sequential there. The bucket is nonetheless contended, because it is a 10-second window and the spec file executed immediately after other files that sign in for real. The repair handles both causes because it observes the state rather than reasoning about who else is running.

ONE THING I FOUND BY OVER-PARALLELISING, REPORTED AS AN ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEFECT. The DEVELOPMENT suite at --workers=4 on this 2-core container fails 6 cases with 'SyntaxError: Unexpected token <, "<!DOCTYPE"' -- the Next dev server returning an error page under on-demand compilation load. At --workers=1, which is what a 2-core CI runner actually uses, the same suite is 118 passed / 24 skipped, which matches CI #180's own development notice exactly. So this is a capacity limit of `next dev` on a small machine, not a product fault, and not caused by this change: auth-rate-limit.spec.ts skips entirely in development.

recommended.title: The fail-closed deployment path is asserted by nobody, because CI runs two of three configurations
recommended.acceptance:
FOUND BY MEASUREMENT IN ROUND 108: the development and production suites were both run to completion and their SKIP LISTS intersected. Five e2e titles are skipped in BOTH, so no configuration this repository executes ever runs them. Two are media-rig rows that correctly need the commander's hardware. THE OTHER THREE ASSERT A FAIL-CLOSED SECURITY BEHAVIOUR: 'a deployment with no identity system - fails closed with 503 and names the operator's remedy', '- publishes nothing only a resolver could know' (playback-session.api.spec.ts), and 'a deployment with no identity system refuses honestly rather than showing an empty list' (watchlist.spec.ts).

They need PRODUCTION MODE WITH NO DATABASE -- the third configuration. ci.yml runs exactly two: development, and production with PostgreSQL. The tests are not broken: run locally in that third configuration the full chromium+api suite gives 62 passed / 56 skipped / 0 failed.

REQUIRED: the third configuration runs in CI and fails the build when it fails.
REQUIRED: the cost is stated rather than absorbed. A third suite run adds to every push; the acceptance is that the fail-closed path is covered, not that it is covered in the most expensive available way. If a narrower invocation -- the three titles, or the two specs -- buys the same coverage for less, take it and say why.
REQUIRED: the three titles actually EXECUTE in the new configuration. Evidence is the run naming them as passed, not a count that went up.
REQUIRED: the two media-rig titles stay skipped and stay reasoned. They are RIG rows in PW-0601's matrix and must not be made to look covered.
REQUIRED: no existing configuration loses coverage, and no skip loses its reason.

OUT OF SCOPE: changing what the three tests assert, and relaxing any of them to make a cheaper configuration reach them.
recommended.notes:
CREATED IN ROUND 108. DEPENDS ON PL-0714 because that task owns .github/workflows/ci.yml and is in REVIEW; editing the file from here while it is an active surface would be the overlapping-surface collision the operating model forbids. Sequenced, not blocked.

THE PATTERN THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF, recorded so the next one is found by a check rather than by accident: scripts/test-validate-repo.mjs ran nowhere until PL-AI-0002; scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and the 30-case Windows lifecycle suite ran nowhere until PL-0714; apps/web/src/components/player/tracks.ts was imported by nothing until PW-0306 wired it. Each time the thing existed, passed, and no gate asked it. A standing mechanical check for 'skipped in every configuration we run' would have found all four, and proposing one is a reasonable thing for this task's implementation to consider -- the measurement that found this was two suite runs and a set intersection.

CONFLICT-CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT FILING: .github/workflows/ci.yml is held by PL-0714 (REVIEW) and by PL-0001, PL-0704, PL-AI-0002 and PW-0312, all DONE. The dependency on PL-0714 is what keeps the two from being active together. The reviewDependencies are read-only here: e2e/tests/watchlist.spec.ts belongs to PL-0715 (REVIEW) and is NOT written by this task.

recommended.title: Install, upgrade, uninstall, reinstall — tested, not assumed
recommended.acceptance: The installer's lifecycle is exercised automatically wherever that is possible on a runner, and everything that is not is named for the commander's machine. REQUIRED: clean install on a machine that has never had the application, then launch. REQUIRED: upgrade over a previous version with user data preserved, which is the one a release breaks most often and nobody tests. REQUIRED: uninstall leaves no service, no scheduled task and no orphaned node.exe, and states exactly what user data it keeps or removes. REQUIRED: reinstall after uninstall. REQUIRED: each case is marked automated or commander-machine, with the reason, so the split is visible rather than implied.
